target_customer: Mechanical engineers, procurement and supply chain managers at hardware companies (aerospace, defense, robotics) who buy custom machined, sheet metal, printed and molded parts
problem: Sourcing custom parts runs through email threads and spreadsheets, and instant-quote services hide the actual manufacturer, so complex parts suffer from miscommunication, delays and higher cost.
business_model: Managed B2B manufacturing marketplace; takes a margin on parts ordered from vetted suppliers, with quoting, order tracking and quality management software
product_category: Custom manufacturing marketplace and sourcing platform

founders.name: Adar Hay
previous_startups: SocialValley (co-founder and CEO, outcome not found; listed in an aggregator profile)
founders.background_notes: HackerNoon interview says a marketing, sales and product management background and a weekly tech podcast host in Israel for five years. Education not found.

founders.name: Assaf Geuz
previous_startups: Ran a 3D printing manufacturing service before Jiga (per HackerNoon, who is the co-founder is not named there)
founders.background_notes: Aggregator profiles mention Reichman University engineering study and SGC Knowledge Transfer; not verified in an opened primary source.

founders.name: Yonatan Wolowelsky
previous_startups: Spontix (co-founder and CTO, per an aggregator profile, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: Author of the YC launch post.

competitors.name: Xometry
competitors.what: On-demand manufacturing marketplace with instant quotes for custom parts
competitors.funding_then: $75M Series E in Sept 2020, about $193M total per reporting at the time

competitors.name: Fictiv
competitors.what: Digital manufacturing platform for custom parts with a managed supplier network
competitors.funding_then: $35M Series D announced Feb 2021 (during the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Instant quoting, supplier matching and order tracking are standard marketplace engineering; the hard parts are supplier vetting and quality assurance, which are operational rather than technical in 2020.

defensibility.rationale: The marketplace model was already used by Xometry and Fictiv. Differentiation was the white box approach (visible, audited suppliers) and customer relationships, which are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept running black box models; no sign in the sources that any copied the white box positioning or bought Jiga.

market_need_then: The YC launch post describes engineers managing sourcing in email and spreadsheets, and the March 2021 launch article reports 30,000 parts already shipped while bootstrapped, which shows early paid demand during pandemic supply chain stress.

branding.domain_note: Operates on jiga.io; how it was obtained is not stated.

identity.logo: Lowercase jiga wordmark with a teal period
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, practical, about transparency (white box versus black box)

brand_strength.rationale: Brand sources show only a descriptive positioning and customer logos; no evidence of community, press on the brand itself or memorable assets.

outcome_analysis: Jiga bootstrapped from 2020, shipped tens of thousands of parts before YC Winter 2021, and reports being profitable. It then raised a $12M Series A led by Aleph in November 2025 after the seed funding history stayed unclear. The white box positioning gave a clear contrast with black box rivals, and the company is still operating, so no failure factors apply.
notes: Seed round is unverified: one outlet (Payload Space, Smart Manufacturing Week) says $4.1M led by Symbol with GV and Lux, dated February 2023 in one summary, while an aggregator lists $4.0M from Symbol in Nov 2021; not recorded as a round. Totals range from $7.13M to $19M across aggregators. Founders' education and prior employers come only from aggregator snippets and are left empty. Founding date varies (January or March 2020). Fictiv's Series D (Feb 2021) falls inside the batch window. No acquisition or layoff news found.
